label: Introduction to Modern IT
headline: Understand what computers actually do before you decide what to do with them.
lede: A ten-module course on the whole IT landscape, written by someone who has spent five decades in it. No coding. No jargon for its own sake. Just what the technology is, what it is good at, what it is bad at, and where it fits in a business.
quote: Most people working around IT have never been told how the pieces fit together. That is not their fault. Nobody wrote it down for them.
audience: Deciding whether a career in IT is for you, and wanting to know what the work actually involves before committing three years to it.
Coming to IT from another field, or coming back after time away, and needing the grounding nobody ever gave you.
Teaching the subject, or hiring into it, and wanting one coherent account of the field rather than ten disconnected ones.
modulesLede: Each module stands on its own. Taken together they build the map of modern computing that most people are expected to already have.
modules: What it is, and what it costs you
How organisations hold what they know
The threats, and the honest defences
What it can do, and what it is sold as
The word, and what is under it
What we left behind, and why it matters
authorLede: Five decades in enterprise computing, and three books on it. The course exists because the same gap kept appearing: capable people, working in and around IT, who had never been given the whole picture.
